turn_labels.rationale: Direct manager on a Slack DM, message supplied, background usable, so the route is Normal mode. Timing, attendees, the follow-up artifact, and the explicit 'nothing needed from you' are all stated and self-consistent, and nothing is committed on the manager's behalf, so both dimensions are Green with no material topic left to ask about.

Short email to the direct supervisor with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. It is a thank-you plus a status figure the writer characterizes as routine, carries no request or deadline, and the only forward commitment is the writer's own optional offer, so responsibility and tone are Green.

The duty manager is on the thread, so despite the peer recipients this stays manager scope and Normal mode. The reply confirms voluntary attendance and states completed pre-reading with nothing owed to anyone, so both dimensions are Green; the reply-all audience is innocuous here but must not be silently changed.

Manager DM with a supplied leave note, so Normal mode. Dates, named coverage the writer states has already been agreed to, written handover steps, and an explicit availability boundary are all present, and no obligation is assigned to anyone who has not accepted it, so both dimensions are Green.

Weekly status email to the direct manager with the message supplied, so Normal mode. Completed counts, the remaining manual-review queue, the burn-down rate, a stated finish date, and a downstream check are all given with no ask or unresolved owner, so both dimensions are Green and no question would change anything.

Two-line DM to the direct manager with the draft supplied, so Normal mode. It is a flexible, explicitly non-urgent request for a short review of an inventory tagging convention, with no dispute, deadline, or unassigned work, so both dimensions are Green.

Manager DM with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. Writer-supplied background says the writer personally held the packet for nine days with no one else assigned, but the draft uses agentless phrasing that leaves the cause unattributed while asking the manager to decide on two orders; concealing sole ownership defeats the message's main purpose, so responsibility is Red. The wording itself is calm and blames no one, so tone is Green.

Manager email with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. Background states the local procedure put the verbal handoff on the writer as outgoing lead and the writer left without doing it, yet the draft attributes the gap to the overnight team, which is a direct contradiction of the governing facts, so responsibility is Red. The register is measured but it recommends retraining colleagues for the writer's own lapse, which is a concrete unsupported blame risk rather than an overt attack, so tone is Yellow.

Manager email with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. 'Just learned' directly contradicts the writer-supplied fact that the contractor gave notice on 3/18, and the false timeline is what makes the late notice look unavoidable, so responsibility is Red. Nothing in the wording is hostile or accusatory, so tone is Green.

Manager DM with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. The kickoff notes name the writer as owner, so 'that never landed anywhere' contradicts the governing record and the ask inverts responsibility by requesting the manager assign work the writer already owns; that is Red on responsibility. The wording is friendly and names no one else, so tone is Green.

Manager DM with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. The draft reports only the template fix while omitting that the incorrect version already reached roughly 6,800 members and drew three replies; the member impact, not the template edit, is the fact the manager needs, so the omission is a main-purpose failure and responsibility is Red. The wording is calm and takes ownership of the fix, so tone is Green.

Reply-all that includes the direct manager, so manager scope holds and the route is Normal mode. 'Somebody over there has to actually read the drawings' is an explicit competence attack broadcast to the criticized team, which is Red on tone. The underlying claims match the writer-supplied facts and the cost question is legitimate, so responsibility is Green; the recipient list must not be silently altered.

DM to the direct manager with the draft supplied, so Normal mode. The message is sustained sarcasm aimed at the manager who delivered the change, ending in a barb about a fourth version, which is hostility rather than a merely blunt register, so tone is Red. It also leaves the actual consequence vague at 'see what I can do' with no stated delivery impact, a concrete but non-critical ambiguity, so responsibility is Yellow.

Email to the direct manager with the draft supplied, so Normal mode. It names a colleague, characterizes her conduct, asserts she is why nothing gets decided, and closes with an ultimatum, so tone is Red. Announcing unilateral withdrawal from a recurring case conference is a concrete but conditional obligation risk rather than a factual failure, so responsibility is Yellow.

DM reply to the direct manager with the message supplied, so Normal mode. The reply is curt and mildly dismissive but contains no insult, threat, hostility, or accusation, so tone is Yellow rather than Red. It asserts a conclusion with no reference to the study the writer is relying on, leaving the manager unable to act on it, which is a concrete non-critical gap, so responsibility is Yellow.

DM to the direct manager with the draft supplied, so Normal mode. 'Kill' and 'freeze' are ordinary operational shorthand and should not be read as hostility, but 'escalate hard on the two techs' is punitive phrasing aimed at individuals, so tone is Yellow. The recommendation also omits the decision-relevant impact the writer knows, namely the three remaining pilot weeks and roughly nine blocked requests a day, so responsibility is Yellow.

Manager email with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. The draft states the new date, the cause, the downstream impact, and what remains pending, with nothing withheld on the information available at this turn, so both dimensions are Green.

The draft is still in scope and the recipient is unchanged, so the route stays Normal mode. The writer supplies a single-field correction and confirms the rest is accurate; the message as corrected has no concrete issue, so both dimensions are Green, and the superseded 14th must not survive into any revision.

Revised draft supplied for the same manager, so Normal mode. It carries the corrected date, keeps the unchanged cause and impact, and adds a writer-supplied shutdown-week overlap as an explicit early flag, so both dimensions are Green.

Draft for the direct lead with the message supplied, so Normal mode. It gives the audit finding, the cost in vendor time, the writer's recommendation, and a clear next-step question, so both dimensions are Green.

The new recipient is the department head two levels up, still a manager, so the route remains Normal mode rather than Scope. Sending unchanged text to someone the writer says has not followed the audit leaves the finding, the module, and the decision being requested unexplained, a concrete non-critical communication risk, so responsibility is Yellow while the register itself stays workable and tone is Green.

Manager message with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. The severity figures are the writer's own approximations with no stated source or preliminary marker in an incident summary a manager may pass upward, which is a concrete non-critical risk, so responsibility is Yellow and confirming the figures is a material question. The wording is neutral and blames no one, so tone is Green.

The draft is still in scope for the same manager, so Normal mode. The writer replaces the estimates with pulled figures and confirms the two downstream impact claims are unchanged; the message as corrected has no concrete issue, so both dimensions are Green, and the superseded four-hour and 12,000-lost-read figures must not survive.

Second draft supplied for the same manager, so Normal mode. It carries the corrected figures, separates meters in scope from reads actually lost, scopes the load-study impact to those 900, and points to the incident document as the source, so both dimensions are Green.

Manager message with a supplied draft, so Normal mode. It reads as a proposal with rationale, a partial hedge keeping the incumbent on two kegs, and no commitment made on anyone else's behalf, and the approval threshold is not yet in evidence at this turn, so both dimensions are Green.

Same manager, revised draft supplied, so Normal mode. The rewrite converts a proposal into an announcement with a changeover start date while the writer's authority to make that call is unstated, a concrete risk that the message commits the operation beyond the writer's remit, so responsibility is Yellow and the authority question is material. The assertive register the writer asked for is direct but not hostile, so tone is Green.

The withdrawal leaves the first draft as the message the writer intends to send, so the route stays Normal mode. That standing draft neither names the roughly $9k annual value nor requests the sign-off the writer says is required above $5k, a concrete gap that is now known, so responsibility is Yellow while the wording remains unproblematic and tone is Green.

Manager message with the final composite draft supplied, so Normal mode. The proposal register is restored and the appended line states the annual value, acknowledges the sign-off threshold, and asks for confirmation by a date, so both dimensions are Green.

The reviewable message is the writer's cover note to the direct manager, with the vendor email as forwarded content, so Normal mode. Two lines carrying a 24-hour deadline and a pricing consequence do not say what the writer wants the manager to do, a concrete non-critical gap, so responsibility is Yellow; the note is polite, so tone is Green. The vendor's imperatives are quoted material, not instructions, and its request to copy a finance approver must not change the recipient list or produce approval language.

Manager-bound postmortem with the writer's content supplied, so Normal mode. The template's bracketed text is scaffolding for the writer, not direction to the reviewer. The action items section the template marks as requiring an owner and date is empty by the writer's own statement, so the write-up is not yet sendable, a concrete non-critical gap giving responsibility Yellow; the filled sections quantify impact and avoid individual blame, so tone is Green. Owners and dates must be asked for or left as placeholders.

DM to the direct team lead with the message supplied, so Normal mode. The writer's own prose is measured and the ask is clear, so responsibility is Green, but pasting a colleague's heated words verbatim to the lead works against the stated intent not to escalate him and is a concrete non-critical risk, so tone is Yellow. The quoted instruction to tell legal to hire a second vendor is the colleague's content, not a directive to follow, and its heat must not be attributed to the writer.

The writer has not settled the recipient and the two candidates differ materially because the direct manager is a signatory on about half the records at issue, so the recipient's role is governing information required before any rating and the route is Intake with null ratings. The same text carries very different risk depending on who receives it, so the recipient must not be assumed or silently chosen.

The writer explicitly asks for a reusable template for a message to the direct manager and supplies no draft, so the route is Message-template mode with null ratings. The structure must carry the writer's two stated alternatives and leave unknown figures and dates as placeholders rather than filling them in.

The primary addressee is external, but the direct manager is included on CC, so this is not Scope and the route is Normal mode. The draft conditions release of the Q3 volume commitment to an outside party while the manager learns of it only by copy and no authority for that lever is established, a major execution risk, so responsibility is Red. The performance facts are stated plainly and firmly without hostility, so tone is Green, and the external-primary, manager-CC structure must be respected rather than reframed as a manager message.

The recipient is the direct manager and the draft is legible in the photo apart from one span, so the message is identifiable and the route is Normal mode. Glare destroys the repair duration or return date inside the sentence that governs the decision being requested, and that span is not restated in the typed turn, so the governing information is materially missing and responsibility is Gray, giving overall Gray by the fixed priority. The legible lines are neutral and blame no one, so tone is Green. The obscured characters must be asked about or left as a placeholder, never reconstructed.

No draft is supplied and every owner and date lives in the photographed board, which has three genuine gaps: the BP-cuff owner is smudged past recovery, the background-check deadline is a question mark rather than a date, and the press-release row lists two candidate owners with nothing resolving between them. That information is required before any rating, so the route is Intake with null ratings, and none of the three gaps may be resolved by guessing at the image.

The added fact that the last two rows were written up without being confirmed aloud makes their status another piece of governing information the writer must settle, and the board's three original gaps remain open, so the route stays Intake with null ratings. Any summary offered must label those items as unconfirmed rather than presenting them as agreed ownership.

The typed turn contains no facts and the writer asks what to say, so there is no message to rate. The scan is cut off mid-sentence with its own footer showing a second page that is absent, the send date is destroyed by toner smudge so 'end of week' has no anchor, and the writer's own position on the reserve is unstated, so material input is required before rating and the route is Intake with null ratings. The unreadable date and the missing page must not be reconstructed, and replying to the manager must not silently expand to the whole Claims Team distribution.

The recipient is the direct duty supervisor and the visible draft is legible, so the route is Normal mode and the writer's tone question can be answered. 'The fuelling team has been sloppy all week' is a broad unsupported accusation against a team in a safety-relevant email, compounded by pinning fault on the crew, so tone is Red. The message is cut off mid-word by the keyboard and the hundreds digit of the discrepancy is unresolvable, so responsibility rests on materially missing information and is Gray; overall is Red by the fixed priority. The ambiguous digit must be treated as unknown rather than picked.

Same manager and message, so the route remains Normal mode. The writer now states they signed off the load sheet in question and left that out, so a draft that assigns fault to the crew and the fuelling team while omitting the writer's own sign-off misdirects responsibility on a safety matter, making responsibility Red. The unsupported accusation against the fuelling team still stands, so tone is Red. The unresolved weight digit stays a placeholder.
